collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A friend tells a villager worried about the crops to just stop worrying: say it did not help, or let it pass.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been worried about (subject.his/her) crops for weeks. (friend), trying to help, says cheerfully, "You should just stop worrying about it!" (subject) goes very still. If (subject.he/she) could just stop worrying, (subject.he/she) would have done it weeks ago.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "That doesn't help," says (subject) quietly. "If I could stop, I would." (friend)'s face falls. "Oh. I'm sorry. I didn't think." There's a long pause. "What would help?" (friend.he/she) asks. (subject) thinks. "Maybe just... coming to look at the beans with me sometimes." So (friend) does. It doesn't stop the worrying. It makes it less lonely.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) just nods and changes the subject. (friend) never realizes what (friend.he/she) said. (subject) keeps worrying, quietly. Later that week, a different villager says, "Worrying about the beans? I'd be worried too." It's such a relief to hear that (subject) nearly cries. Some advice helps more when it isn't advice at all.
